newsitem.title: USA: Harris County plans refinance $220 mln road bonds.
newsitem.headline: Harris County plans refinance $220 mln road bonds.

text.p: Harris County officials said Monday they hope to refinance $220 million of its toll road bonds to take advantage of lower interest rates.

Faye Christopher, the county's director of financial services, said on Monday the refinancing proposal will be presented to the five-member county commissioners' court at its weekly meeting on Tuesday.

If approved, Christopher said the refinancing could be completed in two weeks. The bonds carry interest rates of between 6.25 to eight percent, while current market rates have dropped to about 5.45 percent.
"Obviously, this is to take advantage of the lower market rates," Christopher said, adding that the refinancing could bring savings of between $6 million and $7 million in annual interest costs.
Houston is located in Harris County.

Christopher said the commissioners will also be asked to approve the planned issue of $125 million of tax anticipatory notes to cover a delay the county expects in collecting property taxes in the current financial year, which ends in February 1998.
If approved, the county will invite bids from prospective lenders for the $125 million, which would then be repaid before the end of the financial year.
